title: Birational locally finitely presented separated maps are isomorphisms over a dense open
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism] that is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose $X$ and $Y$ each have finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] and $f$ is birational: it maps the generic points of the irreducible components of $Y$ bijectively onto those of $X$ [def-sc-generic-point], and the induced homomorphism $\mathcal O_{X,f(\eta)}\to\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ is an isomorphism for each such $\eta$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Then there is a dense open subset $V\subseteq X$ such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-birational-common-dense-opens] to $f$. Its finite-component, locally-finite-presentation and generic-local-ring hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses here; it requires no reducedness. Obtain dense open subschemes $U\subseteq Y$ and $V\subseteq X$ for which $g=f|_U:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$. Put $W=f^{-1}(V)$ with its open subscheme structure. Since $f(U)\subseteq V$, the inclusion of $U$ in $Y$ factors as the open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow W$ followed by $W\hookrightarrow Y$.

source.place: Tag 0BAC, lemma-birational-birational, alternative (2); formation of the restricted target

proof.text: The restriction p = f ∣_ V is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change]. Its composite with the open inclusion j : U → W is g, an isomorphism and hence a closed immersion. The Mathlib lemma IsClosedImmersion.of_comp (the general form of [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]) therefore makes j a closed immersion. Equivalently, composing j with the inverse of g gives a section of p, whose closed immersion property transfers back to j along g. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], the range of j is closed in W. Scheme.opensRange_homOfLE identifies that range with the preimage of U under W → Y.

source.place: Tags 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence), 01KT (lemma-section-immersion); separated-case shortening of the argument in Morphisms 0BAJ

proof.text: Pull back the dense subset U of Y along the open map W → Y, using Dense.preimage. This makes the range of j dense in W. Since Step 2 makes it closed, every point of W belongs to U, and U = W as open subsets of Y. The open subscheme structures agree by [def-weil-open-immersion]; rewriting Scheme.Hom.resLE with this equality identifies g with f ∣_ V. The open V is dense in X. No nonemptiness hypothesis is used, so empty schemes are covered.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ, conclusion; elementary density argument after the closed-section calculation
